lists.name: Juno Awards: Album of the Year

podcast.body: Released in 2009, this album featured "Rusted from the Rain" as one of its singles, which was the band's first charting number one. The album was produced by Brendan O'Brien, recorded in Atlanta and Toronto, and took 40 days for recording and mixing in Atlanta. The label (Warner US) initially sought an "A-level" producer like Butch Vig or Brendan O'Brien for the album. The band felt it was a "rock record" compared to their first two "punk" records. Despite the band's confidence, the album was leaked three months before its release and Warner US decided not to release it two months before, forcing them to quickly sign with Roadrunner Records. This last-minute change and the leak "sabotaged" the record's release, though it still performed well in Canada and Germany. It's described as a "polarizing record" for fans, often considered a "grower." "Billy Talent was arrested for the rain, one of the singles from their 2009 album, Billy Talent 3."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This was the band's third studio album, produced by Brendan O'Brien. The production involved spontaneous additions like xylophones and background vocals, which O'Brien would improvise and tuck into the mix. This approach taught the band that not everything needs to be perfectly calculated during recording.
